title: IT Act ss. 22–27 — Income from House Property (Annual value determination) (IT Act ss. 22-27)

content.overview: Section 22 charges the annual value of a building or land appurtenant owned by the taxpayer, unless the property is used for the owner's business. Annual value is the sum for which the property might reasonably be let, with the enacted treatment of actual rent, vacancy and unrealised rent. Municipal taxes paid by the owner are deducted. A standard deduction and interest on borrowed capital are allowed as enacted. Ownership is the gate. A tenant is not charged under this head on the same property.

enhancement.legalPrinciple: Ownership is the gate. A tenant is not charged under this head on the same property.
essentialIngredients: Not used for the owner's business
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 23 determines annual value. A self-occupied property has the enacted nil or limited annual value. Vacancy and unrealised rent are deducted where the conditions hold. Section 24 allows the percentage deduction and interest on borrowed capital, with a cap for a self-occupied house as enacted. Co-owners are assessed on their shares. More than one self-occupied property is not given the same concession unless the section allows it.
examples: The owner lets a house and pays municipal tax.
Annual value is computed and the tax and section 24 deductions are allowed.
The owner's office occupies the building.
